deep.reconstruction:
The page contains no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is a short bibliographic memorandum headed 'Zu lesende Bücher:' (books to be read). The rest of the leaf is blank apart from archival foliation: a circled '176' and a faint pencil '119'. Entry by entry, with my identifications:

(1) 'King. The Life of John Locke. London. 1829.' This is Peter King, 7th Baron King, The Life of John Locke, with Extracts from his Correspondence, Journals and Common-place Books (London: Colburn, 1829). It is history of philosophy and science.

(2) 'Beer. Abhandlungen in Pogg. Ann.' These are August Beer's (1825-1863, Bonn) papers in Poggendorff's Annalen der Physik und Chemie. They include the 1852 absorption-law paper and work on optics, elasticity and electrostatics.

(3) 'Waller. Life of Hooke.' This is Richard Waller's 'Life of Dr. Robert Hooke', prefixed to The Posthumous Works of Robert Hooke (London 1705).

(4) 'Soemmering. [title]'. The title is a hasty scrawl. Given the companion entry on the mind-body union, the most likely reading is S. Th. von Sömmerring, Über das Organ der Seele (Königsberg 1796), on locating the 'seat of the soul' in the ventricular fluid. This identification is mine and not certain from the image.

(5) 'Fagnani. Giornale de' letterati d'Italia. tom. 34.' This refers to G. C. de' Toschi di Fagnano's contributions to the Venetian Giornale de' letterati d'Italia. His lemniscate and elliptic-arc papers appeared there in the 1710s-1720s and were later collected in Produzioni matematiche (1750). These are the historical source of the addition/doubling theorems for elliptic integrals. The reference fits Riemann's interest in elliptic and abelian functions, although it sits in a natural-philosophy bundle.

(6) 'Cauchy. Comptes rendus 1839 (Opt...)'. This points to Cauchy's numerous notes on optics in Comptes rendus 1839. They cover the theory of light, dispersion, metallic reflection and elliptic polarization.

(7) 'Guhrauer. Inaug. Diss. Berol. 1837. (Leibnitii doctrina de unione corporis et animi)'. This is G. E. Guhrauer's 1837 dissertation on Leibniz's doctrine of the union of soul and body.

The list reflects Riemann's naturphilosophische reading on three fronts: the mind/soul-body problem (Sömmerring, Guhrauer/Leibniz), the history of 17th-century science (Locke, Hooke), and optics/ether physics (Beer, Cauchy). There is also one historical mathematical source (Fagnano).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely a list of books to read, with no derivations. The topics (Leibniz on mind-body, Sömmerring's 'organ of the soul', Cauchy's optics, Fagnano) are consistent with Riemann's known naturphilosophical and mathematical interests, as reflected in his published philosophical fragments. It adds only minor biographical/bibliographic detail.
transcription_corrections: The Soemmering title is not legible as 'Denkschriften ... Organ'. It is an unclear scrawl, plausibly a short form of 'Über das Organ der Seele' (1796); treat as uncertain.
'Giornali de' literati d'Italiae' as written in the manuscript corresponds to 'Giornale de' letterati d'Italia'. The transcription's normalization is acceptable.
In the Cauchy entry the parenthesis begins 'Op...' (Optik/optique); the remainder is illegible. Keep '[?]'.

Guhrauer entry: the word after 'Diss.' appears as 'Berol.' (Berolini); a cancellation is possible but not certain. Riemann's Latin reads 'Leibnitii doctrina de unione corporis et animi' and the parenthesis is not closed.
Archival marks are not transcribed: circled folio number '176' at the right margin and a faint pencil '119' above it.
